newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar closes Friday trapped in narrow range.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar closes Friday trapped in narrow range.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar traded in a narrow five point range on Friday closing at US$0.7078/85 after opening at 0.7076/83.
On the Trade Weighted Index it fell marginally, finishing at 67.69, off one basis point.
"The kiwi has been relatively well supported through the overnight session through London and New York overnight," a Wellington-based chief bank dealer said.

He said the NZ$100 million Eurokiwi issue by the Swedish government, lead managed by Hambros Bank and announced on Tuesday, instilled confidence there would be continued investment demand from offshore.
"Obviously the Aussie has struggled in the last 24 hours or so but we have seen it edge up a bit through Asia," he said.

"The kiwi looks in quite good shape with interest in buying down towards 0.7060-65 and at the top side selling interest up around 0.7090-95, so we are caught in a bit of a range and I think we will be within that range until next week," he said.
